name: cloud-chat
_doc_vendored_engine: CI does NOT run the engine source in 1_cicd/src/scripts — it runs the VENDORED COPY at ./build.sh, from this directory. This key DECLARES that copy relationship so the workflow generator can enforce byte-identity (cloud-android-ship-repo-workflow-engine.sh, step 'verify engine ↔ vendored build.sh parity') and go red on drift. Editing the engine alone used to change nothing at ship time, silently — which is how the ABI gate and the GHCR auto-delete gate came to exist only in the file nobody executes. Re-sync with: cp 1_cicd/src/scripts/<engine> ./build.sh

chat.tracker_dir_note: flattened 2026-08-29 — the vendored source now sits at the app root, matching every other app in this repo instead of hiding under upstream/. upstream_repo/pinned_tag stay provenance only; bump pinned_tag + re-run materialize-fork to re-vendor a newer tag. Note: the fork's provenance patches moved to fork-patches/, because patches/ at the RN project root belongs to patch-package, which postinstall runs.

build._doc: Mattermost Mobile (React Native). 'command' is a shell snippet run from the fork root; build-fork runs it via the nix devShell for correct node/ruby/cocoapods. apk_glob captures the output. resign_unsigned=true means build-fork runs apksigner after aligning (RN builds can't embed constellation keystore easily). 'sync-on-open — prevents 20+ react-native arm64+x86_64.'
prepare: [ -f android/app/debug.keystore ] || keytool -genkeypair -v -keystore android/app/debug.keystore -storepass android -keypass android -alias androiddebugkey -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000 -dname 'CN=Android Debug,O=Android,C=US'
build._doc_debug_keystore: The React Native template's android/app/debug.keystore is matched by the repo-wide '*.keystore' ignore, so it exists on a developer disk and has never been in the repo. CI then died at ':app:validateSigningRelease' - "Keystore file .../debug.keystore not found for signing config 'debug'" - because Mattermost's release buildType falls back to the debug config. Generated here rather than vendored, which is what the gitignore's own note says keystores must be. It is the standard, public AOSP debug identity and it never reaches the shipped artifact: signing=resign_post_build + resign_unsigned means build-fork apksigner-resigns the APK with the ONE shared constellation key afterwards, so this throwaway key only exists to satisfy gradle's validation.

modules._doc: Shared modules android/settings.gradle includes BY REFERENCE. Declared so the ship workflow watches them and the publish gate hashes them: a change to any of them must rebuild Cloud Chat, not ride along unshipped. `dir` is relative to THIS file (the app root); android/settings.gradle names the same directories as literals relative to its own rootDir, one level down (upstream's file, not a loop over this map).

gh_release._doc: Rolling GH release 'latest' (shared across the ea_cloud-* apps; each contributes a distinctly-named APK asset), overwritten every main push so https://github.com/diegonmarcos/cloudy-u-android/releases/latest/download/cloud-comms-chat.apk stays stable. Published by `build.sh gh-release-fork chat` (ship-cloud-chat.yml), which uploads dist/cloud-comms-chat.apk with --clobber. Consumed by aa_cloud-superapp ui.external_apps[cloud-chat].install_apk_url. The immutable timestamped per-build release (RSS notification) is separate and stays --latest=false.

analytics._doc: Consumed by :libs:analytics, which reads THIS file at build time and bakes the values into BuildConfig. NOTE: this is a React Native app — its gradle rootDir is android/, so the module resolves this file via ../build.json (see android/settings.gradle).

configs_pages._doc: Configs > General and Configs > About (libs:ui-nav-bars fleetconfigs, rule 1_cicd/src/data/configs-pages.json, #1352 v2). general.sections: the anchors of the one General page, in order (perms, battery, storage, notifications, ui, language are required; app opens this app's own Configs; update is added after perms by default). about: the hand-written part of the extensive About: tagline, description, features, screens, guide, privacy, backends (ids of ac_cloud-account/build.json::fleet_endpoints, resolved to mesh URLs at build time), related fleet apps, credits for a fork. Permissions, data stores, crash/analytics libs, name, icon, version, build sha and date, repo, licence, origin, crash sink, debug API and changelog are derived, never typed here.

about.tagline: Chat on the owner's own messaging server
about.description: Cloud Chat is the fleet's chat client for the owner's self-hosted messaging server. It handles direct and group conversations, media and file sharing and message notifications, with the account and server address coming from the fleet instead of a public service. It exists so everyday messaging between the owner's people runs on infrastructure the owner controls, with the same updates and crash reporting as every other fleet app.
features: Calls with microphone and Bluetooth headsets
Fleet sign-in instead of a public account
guide: Sign in with the account Cloud Account provides.
Start a chat from the pencil button.
Attach a photo or file with the clip button.
about.privacy: No ads and no third-party trackers. A crash report is saved on the phone and sent only to the phone's own C3 WebServer over loopback; nothing leaves the device unless you share it. Usage analytics are opt-in and off by default; when allowed, events go only to the owner's self-hosted Umami and Matomo. It calls no fleet service: its data stays on the phone.

related.why: Mail, news and tasks beside the chat.
Opens a person's chat in one tap.
Signs in to the fleet and holds the tokens and secrets this app reads.

perms._doc: #1360 every grant this app needs, by libs:perms catalogue id (needs), and the fleet apps that do work for it with the grants THEY must hold (helpers). The ONE declaration: generated into assets/app-perms.json (cloud-android-perms-guard.py --write), drawn by Configs > General > Perms (libs:perms AppPermsSection) with live state, Grant / Open and Grant all, asked at first run (first_run), and reported as 'Missing permission X - Grant' when an operation fails (PermsGate). perms-guard fails when code uses a gated API or another app's engine that is not declared here, or when the manifest and this list disagree.
